objective_for_doctor: A 10-year-old Female patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have sensitive pain, right tonsil pain, and left tonsil pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. I have sensitive pain in my throat—both my right and left tonsils hurt, and it also feels sore around the pharynx and the thyroid cartilage area. I have a clear runny nose or nasal congestion too, and the pain is around 5 out of 10.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—so far it sounds like sore throat with nasal symptoms. Do you have fever or chills, cough, trouble swallowing, or swollen/tender neck glands? Also, can you check if your tonsils have white patches or bad-smelling breath?

I don’t know about fever or chills—I haven’t noticed them. I don’t have a cough that I can say for sure. I do have trouble because swallowing feels painful, but I don’t know about white patches on my tonsils or bad-smelling breath.

Doctor: Do you see any swollen tender lymph nodes in your neck, and is the runny nose/congestion clear vs yellow/green? Also, have you had any recent exposure to strep (school outbreaks) or did symptoms start suddenly within 1–2 days?  
REQUEST TEST: Rapid_Strep_Test (and/or Throat_Culture)  
Doctor: If you can, look in a mirror—do your tonsils look red/enlarged, and do you have small red spots on the roof of your mouth?

I’m not sure about swollen tender lymph nodes in my neck. My runny nose/congestion is clear. I’m not sure about strep exposure from school/daycare outbreaks, and I think the symptoms didn’t start suddenly within 1–2 days.  

I can’t really tell about white patches, small red spots on the roof of my mouth, or whether my tonsils look red/enlarged.

Doctor: I’m going to examine you—right now, do you have any hoarseness, abdominal pain, or a rash (especially pink/red sandpapery), and can you open your mouth wide so I can look for red enlarged tonsils or exudate?  
Doctor: Also, how many days has this been going on, and does swallowing liquids hurt the same as swallowing solids?
I don’t have hoarseness, abdominal pain, or a rash that I can see. This has been going on for a little while, not just 1–2 days, and swallowing liquids hurts about the same as swallowing solids.

Doctor: Thanks—since it’s been going on longer than 1–2 days with clear congestion/runny nose and painful swallowing, the pattern fits viral pharyngitis more than strep. Do you have any fever (≥38°C), tender swollen lymph nodes on the front/side of your neck, or do you notice cough (even mild)? Also, can you tell me your latest temperature if you’ve checked?
I don’t think I have a fever, and I don’t have a known temperature reading. I’m not sure about tender swollen neck glands, and I don’t really notice a cough.

Doctor: I’m going to do a quick focused exam—do you have redness/swelling on the tonsils with any white exudate, and are the cervical lymph nodes (front/side of neck) clearly tender or enlarged?  
Doctor: Also, any difficulty breathing, drooling, or muffled “hot potato” voice, and can you rate the pain 0–10 today?

I can’t see or check my tonsils closely, so I don’t know about redness or any white exudate. I’m also not sure about tender or enlarged lymph nodes in the front/side of my neck. I don’t have difficulty breathing, drooling, or a muffled “hot potato” voice. My pain today is about 5 out of 10.

Doctor: Okay—since you can’t visualize tonsils or neck nodes, the most helpful next step is to confirm whether this is strep vs viral; please get a rapid strep test (and/or throat culture). REQUEST TEST: Rapid_Strep_Test and Throat_Culture.  
Doctor: While we wait, do you have any new/worsening high fever, very swollen neck, or trouble opening your mouth (jaw tightness), and is your runny nose still clear?
Okay, I can get the rapid strep test and throat culture. I don’t have a new or worsening high fever, and I don’t think my neck is very swollen. My runny nose is still clear.

Doctor: Thanks—since you have clear runny nose, no high fever, and no strong neck swelling, viral pharyngitis is still more likely, but we’ll confirm with the rapid strep/throat culture. While you wait, can you tell me: is there any headache, stomach pain, or vomiting, and are your symptoms improving, worsening, or staying about the same?
I don’t have stomach pain or vomiting. I’m not sure about a headache. My symptoms feel about the same, not really improving a lot or getting much worse.

Doctor: With throat pain around 5/10, no fever, clear runny nose, no cough you’re aware of, and no rash/vomiting, viral pharyngitis remains most likely—though we’ll wait for the rapid strep/throat culture results. Are you able to check your temperature now, and do you have any visible mouth ulcers or white spots on your tongue/gums?  
Doctor: Also, any known exposure to someone with strep, and are your symptoms making it hard to drink or causing dehydration (less urination, very dry mouth)?

I can’t check my temperature right now. I don’t know about visible mouth ulcers or white spots on my tongue or gums.  

I’m not sure about exposure to someone with strep. I can drink, but it hurts to swallow so I’m not sure if I’m getting dehydrated—I think I’m still peeing like normal, and my mouth doesn’t feel very dry.

Doctor: I’m going to focus on ruling out strep and any red flags: right now, do you have any visible white patches on the tonsils or back of the throat, and is your neck lymph node area (front/side) tender when you press it? Also, are you having any cough at all or just throat-only symptoms?

I can’t see or check for white patches on my tonsils or the back of my throat. I’m not sure if the front/side of my neck is tender when you press it.  

I don’t really have a cough—mostly it’s throat-only symptoms.

Doctor: Since your symptoms are throat-only with clear runny nose, no known fever, and no cough, viral pharyngitis is most likely, but we still need to rule out strep; did the Rapid Strep test or throat culture come back yet?  
Doctor: Also, on a scale of 0–10, how bad is the pain when you’re not swallowing (rest pain), and do you have any difficulty breathing or drooling?

I don’t have the results back yet—I haven’t heard anything about the rapid strep or throat culture.  

When I’m not swallowing, the pain feels about 5 out of 10, and I don’t have difficulty breathing or drooling.

Doctor: Since the rapid strep/throat culture isn’t back yet, my best working diagnosis based on throat-only pain + clear runny nose + no fever is viral pharyngitis; however, I want to confirm no red-flag findings—do you have trouble swallowing saliva, muffled “hot potato” voice, drooling, or one-sided severe throat pain that’s getting worse?  
Doctor: Also, when did it first start (how many days), and has she had any known exposure to someone with strep or has she had similar episodes recently?

I don’t have trouble swallowing saliva, no drooling, and no muffled “hot potato” voice. I also don’t have one-sided severe throat pain getting worse.  

I don’t remember exactly how many days, but it’s been longer than just 1–2 days. I’m not sure about exposure to someone with strep, and I haven’t had similar episodes recently.

Doctor: Given no drooling/muffled voice, no severe worsening or one-sided escalating pain, and a longer course with clear runny nose and throat-only symptoms, viral pharyngitis is most likely; we can use the pending rapid strep/culture to be sure. Does she currently have a fever she’s aware of (or any measured temperature), and can you confirm the school/daycare context for possible strep exposure?  
Doctor: If the rapid strep is positive, we treat for strep; if negative and she’s otherwise stable, we treat supportively (fluids, acetaminophen/ibuprofen for pain) and monitor. DIAGNOSIS READY: Viral pharyngitis (acute upper respiratory viral infection; strep pharyngitis currently less likely pending test results)

[DDX]
1. Viral pharyngitis
